To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

DING proteins of Pseudomonadaceae are localized on PstS containing appendages, the number and amount of appendages in P. aeruginoa are dependent on the expression level of DING, and the expression level of the DING proteins in PA14 is lower than in MDR25 under phosphate limitation.

DING proteins of Pseudomonos aeruginosa are found on the outer surface of cells, and the number of cells with DING on the outer surface is increased by overexpression of PstS or by phosphate limitation.

P. aeruginosae can form unusual outer-membrane appendages containing both PstS and DING proteins and the number of cells and the amount of the appendages are greater in multidrug-resistant strains compared to the reference strain PA14.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel mechanism of bacterial adaptation to phosphate-limiting environments.
a new aspect of phosphate acquisition in P. aeruginoga and the role of DING proteins in this process.
a new aspect of phosphate signaling in P. aeruginosain which the expression of PstS and DING is controlled by the phosphate status of the environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DING protein is localized on extracellular PstS-containing appendages of both PA14 and MDR25 strains.
the PstS-containing appendages of P. aerugiosa are not only involved in phosphate uptake but also in the regulation of phosphate metabolism and the response to phosphate starvation.
PstS and DING are co-expressed on the same outer-surface appendage of P. aerugionsa and are likely to be involved in phosphate acquisition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PstS-containing appendages of P. aerugionsa are not only involved in phosphate acquisition but also play a role in virulence.
P. aeruginosae can express DING on Psts-containing outer-surface structures and this may have implications for bacterial pathogenesis.

P. aeruginoga can produce appendages with PstS and DING on the outer surface, which can be used for phosphate scavenging, and the abundance of appendages is dependent on the level of phosphate limitation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PstS-containing appendages are not unique to multidrug-resistant strains and may play an important role in phosphate acquisition in P. aeruginosain the host.
the expression of appendages in PA14 can be induced by overexpressing PstS and/or DING.
DING proteins may be important in the pathogenicity of P. aerugionosa and other bacteria that express DING proteins.
